title: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

sense.text:
“And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold”. The fold Christ was speaking to were the Jews in Jerusalem, primarily Judah, Benjamin and Levi. The other sheep are the rest of Israel. “Them also I must bring”, that there may be “one fold, and one shepherd”: the two nations gathered together, the southern and the northern kingdom, under one shepherd, Jesus Christ.

Everything the prophets and our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ spoke about was referred to in what is called today the Old Testament, so every point can be substantiated from it.

“They shall hear my voice.” For all of us there was a time we heard this voice. We heard the word of God, and it brought us to repentance, to change. There was something innate in us that made us acknowledge the word of God by hearing his voice and changing our life.

precepts.why:
“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” The rock of our salvation is Christ.

“For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth”; the sea is his and his hands formed the dry land. “O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the Lord our maker. For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice”.

It is the same thing Christ says in John 10:16: his other sheep “shall hear my voice”. Israel is the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand, and in that time it came down to whether they would hear his voice.

“I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold”. All of Jacob is all 12 tribes. That is the same thing Christ was saying when he said he had sheep not of this fold that he must bring, that there might be one fold and one shepherd.

The prophecy was that all 12 tribes were going to be brought back together. The beginning of it coming to fruition was when Christ came and began to teach, and his dying was the beginning of the 12 tribes being gathered back together. That was what his death was about.

sense.text: “Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me.” Who sent Jesus? The Father, and he sent him to gather the 12 tribes of Israel. Christ did not seek his own will but the will of the Father that sent him.

“Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me”. It was already written in Proverbs that they would seek him early and not find him. When Christ, the apostles and the prophets spoke in the New Testament, their words were reiterating what the Old Testament said, and they could substantiate them with the text.

“Then said the Jews among themselves, Whither will he go, that we shall not find him? will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” The Jews asking were the Pharisees and the chief priests, who had “sent officers to take him.”

The question lets you know they were studied. They understood the prophecies that there was a dispersed: Isaiah 11, Tobit 3, Ezekiel 36. The dispersed among the Gentiles are Israel, scattered among the nations and living as Gentiles, and that is who Christ was sent to gather.

precepts.why: Who sent Jesus? “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He did not seek his own will but the will of the Father that sent him. He was sent from his Father to gather the 12 tribes of Israel.

“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That Branch is Christ. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord”.

“He shall not judge after the sight of his eyes, neither reprove after the hearing of his ears”. That is the same exact thing he said in John 5:30: I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father that sent me.

So what did God send him to do? Verse 12: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” That was God’s will in sending his Son: to gather the 12 tribes of Israel. That is him that sent him in John 7:33.

“When your fear cometh as desolation, and your destruction cometh as a whirlwind; when distress and anguish cometh upon you.” “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me”.

They will not find him. That is what Christ told them in John 7:34, “Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me”: he was speaking what the Old Testament had already said.

“And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.” Who are the Gentiles here? Israel. Remember the Jews asked whether he would go to the dispersed among the Gentiles to teach the Gentiles.

Verse 11 says the Lord “shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”, from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath and the islands of the sea. And verse 12 explains who the Gentiles are: “he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The Gentiles that seek it are the outcasts of Israel, the dispersed.

Why “for the nations”? Because we were going to be scattered in all these nations and live as Gentiles.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

This is the reason Isaiah 11 says he shall set up an ensign for the nations: Israel was going to be scattered among all these nations and live as Gentiles. That is the dispersed among the Gentiles.

“For they obeyed not thy commandments: wherefore thou hast delivered us for a spoil, and unto captivity, and unto death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.” Once again it is Israel that is the dispersed, delivered among the nations for not obeying the commandments.

“And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.” Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered among them, and Israel that he will gather out of them.

“And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.” Israel is the dispersed. This is what the studied men understood when they asked, will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles?

“And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise their children”. Based on the scriptures we know the Jews were going to be dispersed among the Gentiles and live like Gentiles.

Come to the New Testament and it shows Paul going out to find the Jews scattered among these other nations, living like Gentiles, living like strangers, living like heathens, and bringing them back to God. This was the prophecy sent from the Old Testament: the job was to raise up the 12 tribes of Israel again.

sense.text: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Galilee of the Gentiles: and that is proved from the Old Testament, where the same land is called Galilee of the nations. What Matthew records here was already written.

precepts.why:
Isaiah speaks of “the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali”, afflicted “by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.” So the nations also means the Gentiles. What is read in Matthew 4:15 was already recorded in the Old Testament.

When the prophets and apostles spoke, to substantiate the points they were making they had to use what is called today the Old Testament. Whatever they said, they had to be able to justify their sayings with that text. And this leads into Acts 10.

sense.text: Christ “must needs go through Samaria”, to a city “called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Samaria lay north of Judea, north of Jerusalem.

“How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.” Christ asked her for water, but the point is her answer. These Samaritans were Israelites that still lived in the land, our people located in Samaria, north of Jerusalem, and the Jews of Jerusalem did not deal with them.

Why? Because the scripture said Ephraim was joined to idols, let him alone, and God told the northern kingdom, ye are not my people. That is why she said the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.

“If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.” The living water is the word of God, the washing of water by the word. The living water he would have given her was understanding: that the tribes were going to be gathered back together again.

“Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?” That shows she understood she was part of the 12 tribes of Israel. She just knew the Jews had no dealings with them.

“The water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.” He is telling her that the water, the understanding he would give her, would bring about the kingdom, salvation, for them, because they had been disconnected from it for so long.

“Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” This mountain is the mountains of Samaria, mount Gerizim and mount Ebal. When Israel first came into the land, the first place they came into was what would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up there. That is why, when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up there and worshipped. But God called his home Jerusalem, and that is where he set up his temple.

“Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.” A time was coming, 70 AD, when Jerusalem would be toppled, destroyed by the Romans; and the mountains of Samaria did not matter either. Neither place really mattered at that point, so there is no excuse for anybody to believe either one did. Christ was explaining that his purpose was to gather in one the 12 tribes of Israel.

“Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.” When he says Jews, he is talking about all Israel. You really do not know what you are worshipping; there will be no worshipping in the mountain nor in Jerusalem, because the hour comes when the true worshippers will worship God.

We know what God’s will is for his people, and what God’s will is for the nations. Our job is to teach those things, and in teaching them, our job is to gather in one the 12 tribes of Israel.

precepts.why: “Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.” That is why the woman said the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans: the scripture in Hosea said Ephraim was joined to idols, let him alone.

“Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.” He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel. Why? Because they fully went into idolatry. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”.

Then: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Because of his anger at their idolatry, the message to the northern kingdom was, you will not be my people and I will not be your God. Leave Ephraim alone; they have turned to idols. That is why the woman in John 4 said, you Jews have no dealings with us.

But it comes back: “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” What is he saying? I am going to bring you back together again. All the prophets spoke from a place of prophecy, judgment, and eventually redemption. That is what gives us hope to change, to repent. If there were no endgame where we could come out of this, there would be no incentive. But God said, if you turn back to me, in the place where it was said you are not my people, there you will be called the sons of God.

“For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken”. It was already prophesied: God already told them that within 65 years Ephraim, the northern kingdom, would be destroyed. That is what is read about in Hosea 1.

“That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”. You are cleansed by the washing of water by the word, so the living water Christ would have given her is the word of God: understanding.

Paul is made a minister “according to the dispensation of God which is given to me for you, to fulfil the word of God”: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints”. It was hid from ages that the northern kingdom had a part to play in this: to repent and come back.

The ones who did understand were the studied men, many of them Pharisees. That is why they said, will he go to the dispersed among the Gentiles and teach them? They read Isaiah, they read Ezekiel, they read Deuteronomy. The masses did not have what is called today the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchment, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now he gave it to the apostles to teach.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”. That gives them hope: the northern kingdom has an opportunity of repentance, he is gathering back the Gentiles. The secret hid for ages was being revealed to the whole world and would no longer be gatekept. He would send his apostles throughout the earth to teach the people: you are not Puerto Rican, you are not Dominican, whatever byword was given to you; you are the children of Israel. “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom”.

That is what is happening to us now in this present time. The understanding of this Bible, of who we are, was hid for ages. The will of God was hid. But in this hour the true worshippers are waking up.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”. That is why she said, our fathers worshipped in this mountain. “And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.”

When we first came into the land, the first place we came into would be called Samaria, and the first altars were set up there, with all Israel standing “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, to bless the people of Israel. That is why when the nation split, the northern kingdom went back up top and worshipped there: that was the place they worshipped initially. But God called his home Jerusalem, and set up his temple there.

Joshua read every word of the law “before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.” When we came into the land we had a mixed multitude of other nations among us. The blessings went on the children of Israel; the cursings, on mount Ebal, went on all those that came against us. And the strangers, the other nations, were conversant in the laws of God. We taught them how to keep the sabbath day: on the seventh day no work, neither thy manservant nor thy maidservant nor the stranger within thy gates. They had to learn the laws.

sense.text: “The Gentiles had also received the word of God.” The Gentiles are the Israelites that were scattered.

They “that were of the circumcision” were the Jews, Judah, Benjamin and Levi, and they contended, argued, with Peter: “Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” You went and dealt with the heathen Gentiles, Israelites that were cut off. Peter, don’t you remember Hosea? These are no longer God’s people.
“But Peter rehearsed the matter from the beginning, and expounded it by order unto them”. Now Peter began to explain and reason why he was dealing with them, telling them the vision he had.

“When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.” What would cause them to hold their peace? Peter would have had to use scripture to explain the vision: what was written before, in Ezekiel 37 and Isaiah 11, that the northern kingdom would be grafted back in. He had to show them it was not something he came up with; it was written.

The vision was an allegory of the message God was sharing with the people: the time was at hand to wake them up. It was time for them to come in.

“Now they which were scattered abroad upon the persecution that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phenice, and Cyprus, and Antioch”. When some heard this they would not accept it, and they persecuted the believers, the followers of Christ, what are called Christians today. As they afflicted them, the people scattered further out and took this gospel, this understanding, out with them.
Cesarea was on the north coast of the land of Israel, and was named after Caesar. Cornelius was a centurion there, “of the band called the Italian band”.

“A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.” Devout means devout according to the law: Cornelius was a law-abiding man. He kept the laws of God.

In a vision an angel of God came to him and said, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God. And now send men to Joppa, and call for one Simon, whose surname is Peter”. His prayers went up before God because they were joined with alms. The vision given to him was to send messengers to Simon.

Peter “became very hungry, and would have eaten: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance”. In the vision there were fourfooted beasts, and a voice telling Peter, kill and eat, and Peter said he did not eat anything common or unclean. But the vision was not really talking about that. When visions come from God, many times they are an allegory, referring to something else.

“A certain vessel descending unto him, as it had been a great sheet knit at the four corners”. The scriptures substantiate the vision: Israel was that vessel, the vessel wherein is no pleasure, gathered from the four corners of the earth. That is why the nations cannot handle us now: when we speak, we use the Bible to explain itself.

“Wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air.” This is what Peter had to explain to the Jews, those of the circumcision contending with him: the fourfooted beasts, the wild beasts, the creeping things and the fowls of the air are referring to man. The vision was not about animals; it was about man, Israel scattered and living as beasts.

“Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” What was the whole purpose of the vision? To bring us back together: to gather the northern and southern kingdom, scattered from the east to the west, north and south.

Rise: it is time, Peter. Awake. Now it is time to gather the 12 tribes of Israel. But before we gather them, we first have to kill: kill the old man, the old mindset, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Then eat: study, learn the scripture, devour wisdom to understanding, so you can teach the northern kingdom. Then go out and teach, go out and prophesy.

In that time there was no New Testament, so Peter would have had to explain all this to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

“Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” Peter understood that common was evil. In other words: I have never done sin, I have never dealt with sinners, with people that were evil.

“What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common.” What would God have cleansed? The subject matter is man: Israel, whom God said he would cleanse and gather back together. To explain that cleansing to those of the circumcision, Peter would have had to use the Old Testament.

“Now while Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean”. He pondered what the Lord was talking about: is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? No, Lord, I have never eaten anything unlawful. God speaks by similitudes: it shows you one thing, but it is really something else.
Cornelius is “a just man, and one that feareth God, and of good report among all the nation of the Jews”, warned from God by an holy angel to send for Peter.

When Cornelius fell down at his feet and worshipped him, Peter told him, “Stand up; I myself also am a man.” Listen, I am a man like you.

“Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” When he came there he came to the understanding that the vision was not talking about food or unclean animals. It was talking about calling another man common and unclean. He came to that because he learned Cornelius was a just man, a devout man.

“Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons”. It does not matter; God does not care whether it is the northern kingdom or the southern kingdom. “But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” That is what Peter came to understand: that Israel, the ones called not God’s people, would one day be joined back in.

precepts.why:
“And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt there”. This is what it means to be devout: devout according to the law, with a good report.

So when Acts 10 says Cornelius was a devout man, he was a law-abiding man who kept the laws of God. “And one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.”

“I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.” These are the angels that bring your prayers before the Most High God, as Cornelius’s prayers came up for a memorial before God.

In the same chapter: “Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.” Prayers are good with fasting and alms and being righteous; that makes your prayers go before the Lord. When you pray to God and combine it with alms and fasting, the prayers are heard before the Most High. That is the same thing read in Acts 10:2 of Cornelius, who “gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway”, and so the angel said, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.”

“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude shows you one thing, but it is really something else that God is trying to explain.

That is what Peter was pondering upon. What is he talking about? Is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? When visions come from God, many times they are an allegory, referring to something else.

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” And “when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” They were coming together for the feast of Pentecost: devout Jews, devout like Cornelius, out of every nation.

Peter understood that God is no respecter of persons. Those that keep the commandments have a place of repentance, in every nation.

“Israel is swallowed up: now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessel wherein is no pleasure.” Now the scriptures substantiate the vision Peter had: Israel was that vessel, a vessel in which nobody had pleasure.

This is why the nations cannot handle us right now: when we speak, we can use the Bible to explain itself. When they hear it they think it is everybody. No. God said Israel was the vessel.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The vessel was knit at the four corners because it was Israel that was scattered through the four corners of the earth, living as beasts, that God was gathering together.

“Let it not be thy will to destroy them which have lived like beasts; but to look upon them that have clearly taught thy law.” So we know the beast is referring to man.

When Peter explained the vision he would have had to refer to scriptures like these: remember, in 2 Esdras it says we lived as beasts.
“So foolish was I, and ignorant: I was as a beast before thee.” In the Psalms it is written that we were as beasts. The beasts of Peter’s vision are men.

“Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the Lord”. The prophet said Israel’s sons would be like a wild bull: these are the wild beasts in the vessel.

“And makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them”. The vision was not about animals, so there has to be a scripture explaining that the creeping things are men. When we were without God, with no ruler, we were like creeping things, like insects or bugs. Without the laws of God we were like beasts, like animals.

“Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria.” “I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven”. The fowls of the air are Ephraim, the northern kingdom.

Imagine those of the circumcision hearing Peter: listen, over here in Hosea he referred to us as fowls. This was what God was showing. Everything must be proven as it is written.

“Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold thy children gathered from the west unto the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of God.” Arise: the same word spoken to Peter. They will rejoice when they remember God, and they are coming from the west unto the east, by the word of the Holy One. That is what will gather the children of Israel back together.

So God was telling Peter: it is time, Peter. Awake. Rise. Now it is time to gather the 12 tribes of Israel.

“Thou broughtest it up with thy righteousness, and nurturedst it in thy law, and reformedst it with thy judgment.” “And thou shalt mortify it as thy creature, and quicken it as thy work.”

That is the kill of the vision. You have to mortify, deaden, kill the old man, and be quickened. Rise, Peter; kill the old man; mortify yourself, discipline yourself, and then go out and teach. In that time there was no New Testament, so Peter would have had to justify it to those of the circumcision from scriptures like this.

“So answered I and said, Swallow then down, O my soul, understanding, and devour wisdom.” That is the eat: you have to go out and learn, study, devour wisdom.

And after you learn: “For thou hast agreed to give ear, and art willing to prophesy”. Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the 12 tribes of Israel back together. Kill, Peter: the old man; mortify yourself. Eat, Peter: devour wisdom. Then go out and prophesy.

“Take it, and eat it up; and it shall make thy belly bitter, but it shall be in thy mouth sweet as honey.” John took the little book and ate it up, and then: “Thou must prophesy again before many peoples, and nations, and tongues, and kings.”

It says the same thing as Rise, Peter, kill and eat: you have to eat, learn, and then you must go out and prophesy.

“There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is common among men”. Peter understood that common was evil. When he said he had never eaten anything common or unclean, he was saying: I have never done sin, I have never dealt with people that were evil.

“Yea, they will give thereof to the common harlots, and deck them as men with garments, being gods of silver, and gods of gold, and wood.” Common is evil. When Peter said he had never eaten anything common or unclean, in other words he was saying: I have never dealt with sinners.

“Neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions: but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.” What God hath cleansed is man: Israel, cleansed of its idols, gathered and brought back together, his people again.

Gathered from where? From among the Gentiles, the nations, the heathen: “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen”, to make the two kingdoms one kingdom. And who? “Take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

This is what Peter would have had to read to those of the circumcision to convince them that the cleansing of the northern kingdom, and its being brought back, was written.

“Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.” And “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

That was the prophecy: in the place where it was said, you are not my people. The time had come, Peter: gather them together, bring them together. And that is happening now. It has been going on since then till now: we are out in South America gathering God’s people, out in Africa gathering God’s people, here in the States bringing God’s people back together.

sense.text: “Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.” He sat down and ate with them, and they said, you sat down and ate with these heathens, these Gentiles, people that are not God’s people. Then Peter began to explain and convince them.

“Then hath God also to the Gentiles granted repentance unto life.” They understood it: God granted repentance to them. The ones Peter sat down with were good; the prophecies show it, the scriptures show it. They have an opportunity.

precepts.why:
James, Cephas and John, who seemed to be pillars, gave Paul and Barnabas “the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” Paul’s job was going to the heathen, the northern kingdom; theirs was going to the circumcision.

“But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.” Paul told him: you already learned this, Peter, and you knew it. God showed you that you cannot call any man common or unclean. You sat with them, you convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, and now you are wavering.

“Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.” Dissimulation is deception, hypocrisy, pretense, deceit: fakery, being fake. “If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?” You are being fake like they were fake.

Peter knew better, because God showed him these people were also able to come into the fold. Rebuked like that, he would be embarrassed, ashamed. But he repented, and as a teacher whose job is to instruct the people, he taught them what he repented from: not to be fake.

“Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently”. This is where Peter taught not to be fake. He came back and taught after he learned: I was wrong. We cannot have fake love for the brethren. God already showed me, and when I was put to the test I was influenced not to accept them. So the message now is: do not have feigned love for the brethren.

sense.text: “When the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.” Devout Jews out of every nation were coming together for the feast of Pentecost.
“And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.” That mighty wind that filled them was the Holy Ghost.

“And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues”: other languages. When the Holy Ghost filled the apostles they were bold in what they were saying, because they knew it was sent of God, and they could prove it.
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Israel was scattered among all nations, as Deuteronomy 28 said we would be.
“Every man heard them speak in his own language”, “in our own tongue, wherein we were born”. That is because we were scattered among the heathen, and we learned their languages.

“Parthians, and Medes”, modern-day Iran; “and Elamites”, India; “and the dwellers in Mesopotamia”, Iraq and Babylon; Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia, Phrygia and Pamphylia, Asia Minor; “in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene”, Africa; “strangers of Rome, Jews and proselytes”, Cretes and Arabians.

The point is that people were being gathered together who were not out of Jerusalem. They were scattered: proselytes, people converting back to the laws of God, those who at one time were without God and were now being brought back into the commonwealth of Israel.

Some understood that they were able to come back, but the masses did not know it. It was the job of the priests and the prophets to teach the people. In the last days God has raised the men back up, and we are going out to raise these people back up and show them they are no longer Arabs and Muslims and African-Americans or whatever byword was put on them: we are the children of Israel.

“For these are not drunken, as ye suppose, seeing it is but the third hour of the day.” “But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel”: “And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh: and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy”.

Prophesy about what? The gathering of the 12 tribes of Israel, teaching the people who they are. The women do it by supporting us, and there were prophetesses that taught the word of God to the children: raising them up in the laws of God, raising their sons up to go out and teach, bringing the people back and gathering the 12 tribes of Israel back in.

precepts.why:
“And when they had prayed, the place was shaken where they were assembled together; and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.” The Holy Ghost was that mighty wind that filled them in Acts 2.

When the apostles spoke and the Holy Ghost filled them, they were bold in what they were saying, because they knew what they were saying was sent of God. They could prove it.

“Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: whilst he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.” “No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.”

While the spirit of God was on him, no word could overcome him. Men, study. When you are out in the street there should be no word that can confound you. We should not be hearing men teaching and not be able to explain basic scriptures. For the most part we are going up against Christians who do not know the Bible. On simple questions we should know who we are and how to explain it. When the spirit of God is on you, no word should be able to overcome you.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” That is the word of God coming upon them. “So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

That is what was happening in Acts: they taught, and the people came in and were gathered. All of you are here because of the word of God being inspired on you, and it was not because the people teaching were shaky. So you men out there teaching, study to show thyself approved.
“There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” The apostles began to speak with other tongues, other languages: there is no speech nor language where their voice is not heard.
